clue.text: Delivery of passage quoted

parts.note: re means concerning or about, standing in for 'of' in the sense 'on the subject of'
a passage quoted from a source is a citation

explanation.surface: A speaker delivering a quoted extract from some text.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitation is a spoken performance of a piece, its delivery to an audience.

clue.text: Work between the lines is inadequate

indicators.note: the work sits between the letters standing for the lines, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RY, railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines of track
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone working between the lines, perhaps reading or writing, is found lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British slang for poor in quality or not up to scratch.

clue.text: Setting to study short passage for the bible

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a text is a short verse from the Bible taken as the theme of a sermon

explanation.surface: A preacher picks out a short Bible passage to study for its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Context is the setting or surrounding circumstances in which something occurs.

clue.text: Setting the path alight while doing pioneering work?

explanation.surface: A pioneer clears new ground, perhaps literally burning a way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, setting fire to a track; figuratively, a trailblazer is an innovator breaking new ground first.

clue.text: Troubles I then get sorted out

indicators.note: the letters of 'I then get' are to be sorted out, that is rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to fix their troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer fills the phrase 'teething troubles', early problems with a new venture, so the clue word stands for the whole phrase it completes.
explanation.definitionFit: Teething troubles are the minor problems that come with starting anything new, the noun teething naming such early difficulties.

clue.text: Available if required, less than one ring needed

indicators.note: the word one appears with less than its full length, its final letter cut off

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A tip about what is needed: just under one ring of the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor on call is ready to attend if summoned, available when needed.

clue.text: Preserve black doorpost

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Instructions to treat a doorpost with dark preservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: A crossing cut short

parts.note: a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: A bridge project abandoned before completion.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, condensing it while keeping its sense.

clue.text: Escaped convict on the other side of the world — he will traverse freely over wild open country first

definitions.text: Escaped convict on the other side of the world

indicators.note: the country comes first, so it is placed before the roamer in the answer

parts.note: the bush is wild uncultivated country, especially in Australia
a ranger is one who ranges, roaming freely over land

explanation.surface: A tale of an Australian runaway who roams the outback.
explanation.walkthrough: In colonial Australia escaped convicts who lived as outlaws in the bush were known by this name; 'the other side of the world' means Australia from a British viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, Australian bushrangers were outlaws, many of them runaway convicts, hiding in the outback.

clue.text: Write inferior articles on the community, chapter for five books

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
tat is cheap, shoddy goods
EU, the European Union, grew out of the European Community

explanation.surface: A writer produces junk about Europe, then a chapter about five books.
explanation.definitionFit: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible, Genesis to Deuteronomy, are known collectively by this Greek-derived name.

clue.text: Most of Hibernian flag

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish

explanation.surface: The bulk of an Irish national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is another name for the iris plant, especially the yellow wild flower of wetlands.

clue.text: What one is doing at Gatwick running away

definitions.text: What one is doing at Gatwick

explanation.surface: A traveller leaving from Gatwick airport is really a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Gatwick is one of London's main airports.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport one boards a plane and departs; to flee is also to escape or bolt.

clue.text: Cover live broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the word live is scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Media coverage of a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a covering, a piece of fabric or anything that conceals.

clue.text: Continental expressing reluctance after no end of gin

indicators.note: the sound of reluctance is placed after the shortened gin
the gin word loses its end, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Hollands is a Dutch gin
er is the hesitant noise of someone reluctant to commit

explanation.surface: A European hesitates after finishing their gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hollander is a native of Holland, a person from the European mainland.

clue.text: Utopian cities laid out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A planner sets out ideal cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic and Utopian both describe aiming at a perfect but impractical vision.

clue.text: Fruit Neil distributed at the meridian

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

indicators.note: Neil's letters are distributed, spread into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Neil hands out fruit somewhere near the line of longitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The International Date Line roughly follows the 180-degree line of longitude, where the calendar day changes.

clue.text: Bird had unnatural growth a very long time

parts.note: a wig is false hair, a growth that is not natural
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A bird suffering from an odd growth for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The wigeon is a species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Certain one of the elements is infallible

parts.note: sure means certain
fire is one of the four classical elements with earth, air and water

explanation.surface: A chemist claims one element never fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Surefire describes something certain to succeed, that cannot fail.

clue.text: One with old bob grieves audibly at trial in Scotland

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
bob was slang for a shilling in old British money, abbreviated S

indicators.note: audibly signals that a word for grieving is heard, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: someone who grieves sighs

explanation.surface: A person with an old shilling groans out loud at a Scottish court.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the pre-1971 British shilling, written s. In Scots law an assize is a trial by jury.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an assize is a trial before a jury, and the word also names the jury itself.

clue.text: Dog among children had been tied up

indicators.note: the dog goes among the children, so it sits inside them

parts.note: seed in the biblical sense means offspring or descendants
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog in the midst of children has been leashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Secured means fastened or made fast, as a rope is tied.

clue.text: Morass of papers about meeting

indicators.note: the papers go about the meeting, enclosing it

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic bog of papers about a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a soft boggy area of land, like a marsh, and figuratively a mess.

clue.text: Short preliminary passage, it follows anthem

indicators.note: it follows the preliminary passage, so it comes after it in the answer

parts.note: intro is short for introduction, a preliminary passage in music

explanation.surface: A short musical opening, then the main anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or chant sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Whale butcher?

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone who slaughters whales should be called a butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is commonly called the killer whale; a butcher, figuratively, is one who slaughters or murders.

clue.text: Positive motivational influence at home I have hiding small amount of money

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a cent is a coin of small value
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A person at home secretly holding a few coins as a spur.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that motivates or encourages a person to act.

clue.text: Not all of machine was needed for strip of wood

indicators.note: not the whole machine word is used, its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal

explanation.surface: Only part of a machine needed for a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin flat strip of wood, used under plaster or in trellis.

clue.text: No end of room for horses!

indicators.note: the room word has no end, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a study is a room for reading or writing

explanation.surface: A complaint about stable space for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a group of horses kept for breeding, or the establishment that keeps them.

clue.text: Pitch by northern lake

parts.note: tar is pitch, a black sticky substance

explanation.surface: Setting up camp by a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in the English Lake District.

clue.text: Does it take to the air and to the water at the same time?

definitions.text: Does it take to the air and to the water at the same time?

parts.words: Does it take to the air and to the water at the same time?
parts.note: a puzzle about a craft at home both aloft and afloat, a seaplane with a hull that lands on water

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that both flies and floats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying boat is a seaplane whose fuselage forms a hull, able to take off from and land on water.

clue.text: Set of rules that's nonsense, fifth-rate

parts.note: cod is British slang for a hoax or nonsense, as in codswallop
E is the fifth grade, after A to D

explanation.surface: Dismissing a set of regulations as rubbish and poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a systematic collection of laws or regulations.

clue.text: Determined position of oddly tainted ore

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of 'tainted ore' are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Finding where some contaminated ore lies.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to establish one's bearings, fixing where something lies relative to surroundings.
